x.label: Autonomy
x.rubric: 0 = takes an action only when asked, one request at a time; 25 = carries out multi-step tasks you start, but stops for approval before anything goes out; 50 = runs a delegated errand end to end on its own; 75 = also works in the background, with routines, watchers or long tasks that follow up and reach out first; 100 = runs around the clock on standing goals, acting for you with minimal oversight

y.label: Context breadth
y.rubric: 0 = two surfaces, such as mail and calendar; 25 = several surfaces within one part of life; 50 = all of one part of life: work (mail, calendar, documents, chat) or home (family calendar, school, chores, groceries); 75 = work and personal life together, including bookings and purchases; 100 = whole life, including payments, health, home and travel

yAlt.label: Distribution surface
yAlt.rubric: 0 = its own app on one platform, which you have to seek out; 25 = its own apps on the web, desktop and phone, but you still go to it; 50 = also reachable through channels you already use, such as email, phone calls or Slack; 75 = lives inside the messaging apps or work tools you already use, with no new app to install; 100 = built into the operating system or the everyday apps billions already use, such as WhatsApp, Gmail or the phone’s assistant

companies.name: Hark
companies.description: AI lab building 'personal intelligence': an app now, its own devices in 2027. Hark Pro, released October 6, 2026 on the web, iOS and Android, is built to be proactive and carries out tasks such as buying groceries, booking a car or building a spreadsheet, with persistent memory. In August Hark showed Handoff, a browser agent for ordering gifts and booking appointments.

founders.name: Brett Adcock
founders.role: Founder & CEO; also founded Figure and Archer Aviation

companies.traction: Hark Pro launched October 6, 2026: free to try, with $20 and $100 monthly plans, and the paid plan free for the first 100,000 sign-ups. Devices are planned for 2027. Multi-year partnership with NVIDIA announced in August 2026.

autonomy.rationale: Hark Pro is built to be proactive and carries out tasks such as buying groceries and booking rides. Scored on its launch materials, since the app is new as of October 6, 2026.

breadth.rationale: Aimed at the whole of a person's digital life with persistent memory; shopping, rides and documents at launch.

distribution.rationale: Its own app on the web, iOS and Android; the devices meant to put it everywhere arrive in 2027.

lastRound.note: Total funding of about $800M counts the $700M Series A, led by Parkway Venture Capital, and the $100M Brett Adcock put in himself when he launched Hark in late 2025 (TechCrunch).

companies.name: Instinct
companies.description: A personal assistant reached by text or phone that connects to email, messaging and other applications. It uses personal context to manage schedules, bookings and everyday errands.

founders.name: Noah Shinn
founders.role: Founder; formerly a research scientist at Sierra

companies.traction: Invite-only since August 2026. Group chats reached early-access users on October 5, 2026: the agent can join a thread with friends who have no account, to plan trips, buy tickets or coordinate carpools.

autonomy.rationale: Works across connected apps and real-world errands, joins group chats to plan and buy, and follows up on its own. Held a notch below the leaders because the product is invite-only and untested outside early access.

breadth.rationale: Email, messaging, calendars and other connected apps plus real-world errands such as bookings, tickets and carpools: close to whole-life.

distribution.rationale: Reached by text and phone with no app, and since October 5, 2026 it joins group chats, even with friends who have no account. That matches the other text-native agents (Pally, Ollie). Rescored from 72.

lastRound.note: $1B Series C at a $10B post-money valuation, announced September 28, 2026; Sequoia Capital, Benchmark and Coatue invested and no lead was named. Total funding of about $1.4B adds this round to the $350M TechCrunch reported through the Series B on August 26, 2026.

companies.name: Town
companies.description: Personal assistant with shared memory across web, email, Slack and phone. It handles connected email, calendar, documents, recurring routines and browser tasks, with permissions controlling which actions it may take.

founders.name: Jean-Denis Greze
founders.role: Co-founder & CEO; former CTO of Plaid

founders.name: Tony Vincent
founders.role: Co-founder; former applied-AI product director at Google

companies.traction: Public product; September updates include voice, presentations, maps and agent-to-agent coordination.

autonomy.rationale: Runs recurring routines and cross-tool tasks in the background, across email, Slack, the browser and phone, within the permissions you set.

breadth.rationale: Aimed at professional life: email, calendar, documents, Slack, phone, browser tasks and maps; payments and home are not described.

distribution.rationale: Reached on the web, by email, in Slack and by phone; mostly through its own surfaces rather than the apps you already live in.

companies.name: Superhuman Go
companies.description: Proactive AI assistant from Superhuman, the company formerly called Grammarly. It runs in the browser, on the desktop and on phones across the apps you already use, offers help without being asked, and through connectors to Gmail, Google Calendar and Jira it drafts replies, sorts the inbox, coordinates meetings and updates documents and tickets. Nothing happens without your approval.
companies.parent: Superhuman (formerly Grammarly) — private, and valued as a writing and productivity-software business rather than as a personal-agent product. Go is one of four products in its suite, alongside Grammarly, Coda and Superhuman Mail.
companies.traction: Launched October 29, 2025 with the rebrand; included in every Superhuman plan, with a free tier. Works as Chrome and Edge extensions, Windows and Mac apps, iOS and Android apps, on the web and in Slack.

autonomy.rationale: Proactive: it looks for chances to help without being prompted, and it can draft, sort, schedule and update across connected apps. But every action waits for your approval (Go suggests, you decide), so it does not act on its own.

breadth.rationale: A cluster of work tools: email, calendar, documents and tickets through connectors.

distribution.rationale: Chrome and Edge extensions, Windows and Mac apps, phones, the web and Slack: it shows up inside the tools you already use.

companies.name: Duckbill
companies.description: Combines AI with human execution for household errands, returns, appointments, gifts and bookings. Its direct consumer app remains available alongside API, MCP and CLI integrations for other agents.

founders.name: Meghan Verena Joyce
founders.role: Co-founder & CEO; formerly Uber and Opendoor

companies.traction: Direct app signup is available; execution infrastructure is also offered to other AI products.

autonomy.rationale: You hand over an errand, such as a return, an appointment or a gift, and it is done end to end, but a human is still in the loop on execution, so the software’s own autonomy is capped.

breadth.rationale: Household errands, returns, appointments, gifts and bookings: broad personal life, though not your inbox or calendar.

distribution.rationale: Its own app, plus an API and MCP that let other AI products hand it errands.

companies.name: folk
companies.description: Personal assistant that lives in iMessage, Telegram and WhatsApp and texts you first. It books tables, watches flights and handles email when asked, runs background watchers, and works through multi-step tasks from its own cloud computer.
companies.traction: Free plan with unlimited chatting and three background watchers; Pro $9.99 a month (folk.com, October 5, 2026).

autonomy.rationale: Editorial estimate: it texts first, runs background watchers on flights and prices, and books tables or handles email when asked; payments and phone calls are not advertised.

breadth.rationale: Messaging, email, restaurant bookings and flight and price watching; no payments or phone calls.

distribution.rationale: Lives entirely inside iMessage, Telegram and WhatsApp, with no app to install.

lastRound.note: Company-level seed for Nozomio Labs, which also builds Nia, a context tool for coding agents, so it is not a folk-only round; announced September 1, 2025 per startup press. An aggregator lists a further $62M round in February 2026 that no company statement or reporting confirms, so it is not counted.

news.title: All the AI agents that can live in your text messages

checks.title: Nozomio Labs location and seed round

companies.name: Microsoft Copilot
companies.description: Microsoft's consumer assistant in Windows, Edge, the Copilot apps and the web. With your confirmation it books restaurants, tickets and travel and buys gifts through partner sites, works across open tabs in Edge's Copilot Mode, and reads your Outlook.com, Gmail, Google Calendar, OneDrive and Google Drive through connectors, with long-term memory.
companies.parent: Microsoft — public (NASDAQ: MSFT). Copilot is one of Microsoft's AI products; the parent's market capitalization is not a standalone product valuation.
companies.traction: Connectors, memory and proactive suggestions arrived in the fall 2025 release. On September 25, 2026 Microsoft merged its consumer and work Copilot apps and announced Autopilot, an always-on agent, in private preview.

autonomy.rationale: Books and buys on your behalf through partner sites and acts across Edge tabs, but every booking or purchase waits for your confirmation, and the always-on Autopilot is still a private preview.

breadth.rationale: Email, calendar, contacts and files through connectors, plus dining, travel, tickets and shopping; no home or health.

distribution.rationale: Built into Windows and Edge, with iOS and Android apps and the web.

news.title: Microsoft Copilot Fall Release Includes Collaboration and Personalization Features

companies.name: Genspark
companies.description: General-purpose AI agent and workspace. Its Super Agent breaks a request into steps and carries them out: it reads and sends email through Gmail or Outlook, works from your calendar, makes phone calls on your behalf to book appointments and reservations (Call For Me), and produces slides, sheets, documents and research.
companies.traction: Grew to about $250M in annualized revenue within a year of its April 2025 relaunch as an agent, per reports. Call For Me places calls in more than 40 countries, through Twilio.

autonomy.rationale: Runs multi-step tasks on its own, including outbound phone calls to businesses and people, and sends or schedules email; you start each task.

breadth.rationale: Email, calendar, phone calls, documents and the web; no payments, home or health.

distribution.rationale: Its own web app, browser and mobile apps; it reaches other people by phone, but you have to come to Genspark.

lastRound.note: The extension follows a $275M Series B at $1.3B in November 2025, led by Emergence Capital. Dealroom reports total funding of more than $645M.

news.title: Genspark raises $100M Series B extension at $2.6B valuation
